table_invariants: snapshot_id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(); voice_session_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES voice.session(voice_session_id); UNIQUE (voice_session_id, session_version) identifies the stored revision.

resource_scope_id, route_profile_version, lease_epoch, input_epoch, media_epoch and turn_id are mandatory context fields; this candidate-dialogue record is not a qualified booking draft, confirmation or consent proof.

content_key_version, content_nonce, content_ciphertext and content_auth_tag store server-encrypted content; retention_expires_at is mandatory. Transactional authority, deduplication, authenticated context, expiry and governed retention behavior remain application/schema verification obligations, not claims certified by this allocation entry.

voice.dialogue_snapshot_purge_receipt: voice_session_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES voice.session(voice_session_id), session_version integer NOT NULL, input_epoch/media_epoch/turn_id mandatory identity, retention_expires_at (the purged row's own original value) and purged_at mandatory, PRIMARY KEY (voice_session_id, session_version). Bounded, non-content acceptance metadata only, written in the same transaction as deleteDialogueSnapshot's DELETE (AUDIT-VOICE-APPLICATION-WIRING-20261003 R4-resolve governed purge loses accepted-history distinction) -- never dialogue content, never a parallel retention authority.

voice.session gains dialogue_snapshot_history_unavailable_floor integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 (AUDIT-VOICE-APPLICATION-WIRING-20261003 R4-retention purge-receipt lifecycle): a SEPARATE monotonic watermark from dialogue_snapshot_fence_version, raised only when VoiceSessionService.purgeExpiredDialogueSnapshotPurgeReceipts ages a receipt out under the EXISTING voice_booking_evidence evidence policy (no new evidence family registered) -- never a new per-turn table, so the receipt table itself stays bounded rather than accumulating forever.

voice.dialogue_snapshot_purge_receipt_scan_cursor: a single singleton row (id boolean PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT true, CHECK (id)) persisting only the keyset position (purged_at_text, voice_session_id, session_version) VoiceSessionService.purgeExpiredDialogueSnapshotPurgeReceipts stopped at when a scan hit its page bound mid-backlog, so the next invocation resumes past an already-examined held run instead of re-scanning it forever; cleared to NULL once a scan reaches the real end of the eligible backlog so holds released since can be re-checked. Bounded at exactly one row -- no retention policy needed.
voice_application_allocations.description: Versioned encrypted candidate-dialogue snapshots for trusted voice persistence/restoration, reserved by the original audit execution scope; no booking-draft or consent authority is introduced. V0106 also carries a bounded, non-content purge-receipt table so a governed purge cannot be mistaken for proof a write never landed, plus a session-level floor so that receipt's own governed metadata retention can age it out without either reopening its key for write reuse or being mistaken for proof the write never landed.

table_invariants: billing.phase1_remittance_proofs.proof_id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() — server-generated only; no client-supplied identity column.
batch_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES billing.phase1_reimbursement_batches(batch_id) — fixed at insert, never updated (no UPDATE ... SET batch_id path).

driver_id varchar(100) NOT NULL — denormalised from the batch at insert time for ownership checks without a join; must equal the batch's driver_id (enforced in application layer or a CHECK against a computed column, not by trusting client input).
content_hash text NOT NULL, content_type text NOT NULL, size_bytes bigint NOT NULL — set once at insert (immutable content identity); no UPDATE statement may target these three columns.

scan_state text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending_scan' CHECK (scan_state IN ('pending_scan','clean','rejected')) — the only column a scan-worker transition may write, plus scan_completed_at/rejection_reason.
UNIQUE (content_hash) is NOT applied — the same physical proof file may legitimately be re-uploaded/re-referenced across distinct batches; dedupe is a future concern, not this migration's.

billing.phase1_remittance_proof_payment_receipts: receipt_id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), batch_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES billing.phase1_reimbursement_batches(batch_id), proof_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES billing.phase1_remittance_proofs(proof_id), idempotency_key text NOT NULL, UNIQUE (batch_id, idempotency_key) — the idempotency invariant: a retried mark-paid call with the same key on the same batch must read back this row instead of inserting a second one.

Application transaction for mark-paid-with-proof: SELECT batch FOR UPDATE, verify approved_at IS NOT NULL AND proof.scan_state = 'clean' AND proof.batch_id = batch.batch_id, INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (batch_id, idempotency_key) DO NOTHING RETURNING *, then UPDATE batch.status='paid' only when the INSERT actually happened (i.e. this was not a replay) — all within one transaction so a crash between steps cannot leave a receipt without a paid batch or vice versa.
additional_allocations.description: 匯款證明儲存中繼資料、掃描狀態與冪等付款收據 migration

table_invariants: ops.phase1_push_delivery_claims: outbox_id uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES ops.consumer_notification_outbox(outbox_id) — one live claim row per outbox row (not a history table); fence_token integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.

Claim acquisition: UPDATE ... SET worker_id=$new, claim_state='claimed', fence_token = fence_token + 1, lease_expires_at = now() + lease WHERE outbox_id=$1 AND (claim_state != 'claimed' OR lease_expires_at < now()) RETURNING fence_token — an already-live, unexpired lease is never silently reassigned; the caller must observe zero rows updated and back off.

Every subsequent write (release, receipt persistence) is WHERE outbox_id=$1 AND fence_token=$claimedFenceToken — a worker whose lease has since been reclaimed writes with a stale fence_token and its UPDATE affects zero rows, which the caller must treat as claim loss, not success.

ops.phase1_push_delivery_receipts: receipt_id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), outbox_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES ops.consumer_notification_outbox(outbox_id), dedupe_key text NOT NULL, UNIQUE (dedupe_key) — dedupe_key is server-derived from (outbox_id, fence_token), never client-suppliable, so a retried send for the same claimed attempt cannot insert a second receipt.

tenant_id and passenger_subject_ref are NOT NULL on both tables and copied from ops.consumer_notification_outbox at claim/receipt time, not re-derived from caller input, preserving tenant + passenger-subject isolation independent of what a compromised or buggy caller asserts.

device_delivery_state text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown' CHECK (device_delivery_state IN ('unknown','delivered','delivery_failed')) — no application code path may set this to 'delivered' as a side effect of provider_ack_state='provider_acknowledged'; they are independent columns written by independent events.

Persistence-failure handling is an application-transaction concern, not a schema constraint: the service records provider ack results by first executing the fence-checked UPDATE/INSERT inside a transaction; if that transaction itself fails to commit, the caller's return value must be the outcome 'persistence_unknown' (see packages/contracts/src/passenger-push-delivery.ts), never a fabricated 'recorded' outcome — this table design supplies the idempotent target for a retry, it does not itself prevent a caller from mis-reporting a failed commit.
additional_allocations.description: 被動推播送達 claim/lease/fence 與冪等收據 migration；provider 回執與真實裝置送達分離記錄

table_invariants: admin.phase1_platform_adapters: id text PRIMARY KEY, revision integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 — no table existed for this domain before this migration; platform_admin.repository.ts's PlatformAdminState currently covers only tenants/public-info/placards (see support/unblock/SR-ADMIN-ADAPTER-001 planning decision).

credential_expiry_reference text NULL, credential_expiry_expires_at timestamptz NULL — both columns nullable independently of each other and of the row; absent/unrecorded expiry is a valid, distinct state, never coerced to a sentinel value. Never a column for the secret itself.

Optimistic concurrency: every UPDATE is WHERE id=$1 AND revision=$expectedRevision, and the same statement sets revision = revision + 1; zero rows affected means a stale expectedRevision and the caller must surface a conflict rather than retry-and-overwrite.

admin.phase1_platform_adapter_mutation_audit: audit_id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), adapter_id text NOT NULL REFERENCES admin.phase1_platform_adapters(id), previous_revision integer NOT NULL, new_revision integer NOT NULL, reason text NOT NULL — inserted in the same transaction as the adapter UPDATE (both succeed or both roll back), so lastMutationAudit on the returned record is always the row the caller can see, never a promise of an audit write that might not have landed.

The warning-window policy (packages/contracts/src/platform-adapter-registry.ts AdapterCredentialExpiryWarning) is computed at read time from credential_expiry_expires_at against a server-side configured window; it is not a persisted column, so changing the window does not require a migration or a backfill.
additional_allocations.description: Adapter registry 持久化、憑證到期非機密參照與伺服器端稽核 migration

table_invariants: voice.phase1_work_item_repair_audits: repair_id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), work_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES voice.work_item(work_id), request_id varchar(255) NOT NULL, actor_id varchar(100) NOT NULL, reason text NOT NULL, expected_lease_epoch integer NOT NULL, previous_status varchar(20) NOT NULL, previous_attempt_count integer NOT NULL, previous_last_error text NULL, allocated_max_attempts integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 5, created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), UNIQUE (work_id, request_id) — captures durable ops repair authorization with request-level deduplication; never creates a parallel queue.

Repair transaction invariants: repair execution must verify in the same transaction that target work_item is currently status='failed' with lease_epoch=expected_lease_epoch; resets status to 'pending' with a fresh maxAttempts budget, preserving original work_id, payload_ref, dedupe_key, command_id and ordinary-call nullable voice_session_id.

voice.phase1_work_item_attempt_audits: attempt_audit_id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), work_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES voice.work_item(work_id), attempt_no integer NOT NULL, lease_epoch integer NOT NULL, attempt_stage varchar(20) NOT NULL CHECK (attempt_stage IN ('started', 'terminal')), outcome varchar(20) NOT NULL CHECK (outcome IN ('started', 'completed', 'failed', 'fenced')), error_message text NULL, started_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), finished_at timestamptz NULL, created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), CONSTRAINT ck_phase1_work_item_attempt_stage_outcome CHECK ((attempt_stage = 'started' AND outcome = 'started') OR (attempt_stage = 'terminal' AND outcome IN ('completed', 'failed', 'fenced'))), CONSTRAINT uq_phase1_work_item_attempt_stage UNIQUE (work_id, lease_epoch, attempt_no, attempt_stage) — finite append-only attempt event contract with discrete started and terminal stages, duplicate protection, and crash-safe event preservation without UPDATE or DELETE.
Both audit tables are strictly append-only via voice._make_append_only(...) trigger: no UPDATE or DELETE is permitted by any application or repair code path.
Historical data invariant: existing historical work only preserves recorded attempt count and last_error; repair records do not fabricate non-existent historical attempt timestamps.
launch_allocations.description: Voice work_item 補跑稽核、嘗試紀錄與 lease-fenced 修復資料表 migration

table_invariants: reg.phase1_registry_expiry_events: event_id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), scope varchar(100) NOT NULL, entity_type varchar(50) NOT NULL CHECK (entity_type IN ('driver', 'policy')), entity_id varchar(100) NOT NULL, credential_type varchar(100) NOT NULL, source_fingerprint text NOT NULL, source_expiry_at timestamptz NULL, status varchar(50) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'leased', 'completed', 'superseded', 'failed')), attempt integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, run_after timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), lease_token integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, leased_until timestamptz NULL, worker_id text NULL, last_error text NULL, superseded_by_event_id uuid NULL REFERENCES reg.phase1_registry_expiry_events(event_id), superseded_at timestamptz NULL, created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), UNIQUE (source_fingerprint) — dedicated expiry tracking without duplicate driver or policy state.

Deterministic source fingerprint: SHA-256 over canonical UTF-8 JSON tuple guarantees exact source revision uniqueness: driver = ['credential-expiry/v1', scope, 'driver', driverId, sourceFieldName, Date.parse(expiry)]; policy = ['credential-expiry/v1', scope, 'policy', policyId, vehicleId, policyNo, insuranceType, Date.parse(startAt), Date.parse(endAt), status]. Updated_at and derived lifecycle statuses are excluded.
Strict row locking order: source row lock (FOR UPDATE on driver or policy) strictly precedes event row lock, ordered by entity ID in multi-row batches.

Superseded invariant: renewed credentials yield a distinct fingerprint; previous un-superseded events for the same entity and credential type are marked status='superseded' with superseded_at timestamp, preserving historical audit without overwriting original source validity.

reg.phase1_registry_expiry_delivery_intents: intent_id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), event_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES reg.phase1_registry_expiry_events(event_id), scope varchar(100) NOT NULL, idempotency_key text NOT NULL UNIQUE, tenant_id varchar(100) NOT NULL, recipient_email text NOT NULL, from_email text NOT NULL, subject text NOT NULL, body text NOT NULL, delivery_status varchar(50) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (delivery_status IN ('pending', 'enqueued', 'sent', 'failed', 'superseded')), outbox_delivery_id text NULL, last_error text NULL, enqueued_at timestamptz NULL, created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() — immutable delivery intent with concrete trigger-enforced immutability boundary.

Concrete immutability boundary: BEFORE UPDATE trigger reg.enforce_phase1_expiry_delivery_intent_immutability() strictly forbids updates to frozen payload fields (intent_id, event_id, scope, idempotency_key, tenant_id, recipient_email, from_email, subject, body, created_at), while permitting mutable delivery bookkeeping transitions (delivery_status, outbox_delivery_id, last_error, enqueued_at, updated_at).
Idempotency key format: derived deterministically as ['credential-alert/v1', scope, eventId, recipientEmail] to prevent duplicate alert fan-out.

table_invariants: ops.phase1_notification_mail_deliveries: delivery_id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), tenant_id varchar(100) NOT NULL, idempotency_key text NOT NULL, message_id text NOT NULL, payload_hash text NOT NULL, status varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued' CHECK (status IN ('queued', 'sent', 'failed')), recipient_email text NOT NULL, from_email text NOT NULL, subject text NOT NULL, body text NOT NULL, queued_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), sent_at timestamptz NULL, next_attempt_at timestamptz NULL, lease_attempt_id uuid NULL, lease_expires_at timestamptz NULL, attempts jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb, created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), CONSTRAINT uq_phase1_notification_mail_tenant_key UNIQUE (tenant_id, idempotency_key) — durable PostgreSQL storage for OutboxState compatible with MailOutbox.transaction callback.

Idempotency invariant: UNIQUE (tenant_id, idempotency_key) enforces that the same key within a tenant cannot produce duplicate delivery rows. Replaying identical payload returns existing receipt; differing payload throws conflict.

ops.phase1_notification_mail_outbox_lock: lock_key varchar(50) PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT 'mail_outbox_master', locked_by text NULL, locked_at timestamptz NULL — serialization lock row for multi-replica MailOutbox.transaction execution.

Single persisted attempt authority: ops.phase1_notification_mail_deliveries.attempts jsonb is the sole persisted attempt authority for each delivery, mapping 1:1 and losslessly to DeliveryReceipt.attempts: DeliveryAttempt[] (attemptId, attemptNo, startedAt, finishedAt, outcome, errorCode, retryable, acknowledgement). Reconciling uncertain-to-late-sent updates modifies this authority atomically inside MailOutbox.transaction without a redundant secondary attempts table or dual-write divergence.

Separation of provider acknowledgement and inbox arrival: provider acknowledgement is recorded as transport acceptance evidence, never converted to a false assertion of end-user inbox receipt. Late acknowledgements remain associated with their original attempt.

table_invariants: admin.phase1_partner_notification_bindings: entry_slug varchar(150) PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES admin.phase1_partner_channel_entries(entry_slug) — one primary binding per entry in v1 (design §3.1); binding_id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() UNIQUE — the stable id later referenced from delivery contexts, never reused across entries.

tenant_id varchar(100) NOT NULL, partner_id varchar(100) NOT NULL, webhook_id varchar(100) NOT NULL REFERENCES admin.phase1_tenant_webhook_endpoints(webhook_id) — application code must additionally verify entry.tenant_id = binding.tenant_id = webhook.tenant_id and entry.partner_id = binding.partner_id before any dispatch (§3.1); this is not a DB-level CHECK because admin.phase1_tenant_webhook_endpoints carries no partner_id column today.

version integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 — optimistic concurrency: PUT is `WHERE entry_slug=$1 AND version=$expectedVersion` and the same statement sets version = version + 1; a URL/events/owner/secret rotation on the referenced endpoint requires this binding's state to return to test_pending and be re-validated (design §3.1) — the migration provides the column, the transition itself is application logic.

state varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'test_pending' CHECK (state IN ('test_pending','ready','disabled')) — matches PartnerEntryNotificationBindingState in packages/contracts/src/partner-passenger-notification.ts.

purpose varchar(50) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'passenger_notification' CHECK (purpose = 'passenger_notification') — fixed for v1; event_types jsonb NOT NULL holds a subset of the five PartnerPassengerEventType values and must be a subset of the referenced webhook's own `events` allowlist at dispatch time, not enforced by a DB constraint.

acknowledgement_policy varchar(50) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'durable_partner_acceptance_v1' CHECK (acknowledgement_policy = 'durable_partner_acceptance_v1'); validated_endpoint_fingerprint text NULL, validated_at timestamptz NULL — both null until a passenger.notification.test.v1 binding test succeeds; enabling (state -> 'ready') requires validated_endpoint_fingerprint to match the endpoint's current fingerprint, never a stale one.
updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(). Binding mutation reuses the existing tenant-webhook audit path; no separate audit table is allocated by this migration.

mobility.phase1_order_partner_notification_routes: order_id varchar(255) PRIMARY KEY — one immutable route per order (design §4), no history table; tenant_id varchar(100) NOT NULL, partner_id varchar(100) NOT NULL, entry_slug varchar(150) NOT NULL REFERENCES admin.phase1_partner_channel_entries(entry_slug).

partner_user_ref varchar(255) NOT NULL, drts_passenger_id varchar(100) NOT NULL — both copied from the authenticated handoff / admin.phase1_partner_user_identity_links row inside the same transaction that creates the order, never re-derived from a later or self-asserted session; passenger_subject_ref varchar(255) NOT NULL is for internal reconciliation only and must never be copied into the outbound wire payload (design §6).

identity_linked_at timestamptz NOT NULL, consent_bundle_version varchar(50) NOT NULL, notification_policy_version varchar(50) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'partner_notification_v1' CHECK (notification_policy_version = 'partner_notification_v1'), ride_ref varchar(255) NOT NULL UNIQUE — not usable as a bearer credential; unique so a navigation resolve (design §10) cannot be replayed against a different order. created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now().

No route_missing/route_ambiguous/owner_changed row is ever inserted into this table — those are absence-of-route or stale-route outcomes recorded as failure_reason on V0105's delivery context, never a placeholder row here. When an entry's tenant_id later changes, this row is not rewritten; the owner_changed check compares this frozen tenant_id against the entry's current tenant_id at dispatch time.
mobility.phase1_partner_notification_sequences: order_id varchar(255) PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES mobility.phase1_order_partner_notification_routes(order_id), next_sequence bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.

Allocation transaction: `UPDATE ... SET next_sequence = next_sequence + 1 WHERE order_id = $1 RETURNING next_sequence - 1 AS event_sequence`, executed in the same transaction that creates the outbox row (design §5); a retry of the same logical event reuses the previously allocated sequence and must not call this allocator a second time for one event. This table — not the existing in-memory SSE eventVersion counter on PassengerRideAuthorityView (phase1-p5-s3-multi-taxi.ts), which is not durable and resets across reconnects — is the sole durable ordering authority for partner notifications.

table_invariants: mobility.phase1_partner_notification_delivery_contexts: outbox_id varchar(255) PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES ops.consumer_notification_outbox(outbox_id) — one immutable context per outbox row, written before the first send attempt (design §4); never rewritten with a different route/binding/payload for a retry. delivery_id uuid NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() UNIQUE — the deliveryId on the WebhookEventPayload wire envelope, fixed at insert.

order_id varchar(255) NOT NULL REFERENCES mobility.phase1_order_partner_notification_routes(order_id), entry_slug varchar(150) NOT NULL, tenant_id varchar(100) NOT NULL, partner_id varchar(100) NOT NULL — denormalised from the route row at insert time for ownership checks without a join; these four columns must equal the referenced route's values and are never re-derived from caller input.

binding_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES admin.phase1_partner_notification_bindings(binding_id), binding_version integer NOT NULL, webhook_id varchar(100) NOT NULL, endpoint_fingerprint text NOT NULL — the binding/endpoint snapshot at first-attempt time; a later binding or endpoint rotation does not retroactively change an already-created context row.

wire_payload jsonb NOT NULL, wire_payload_hash text NOT NULL — the exact PartnerPassengerNotificationWirePayload (packages/contracts/src/partner-passenger-notification.ts) already sent or about to be sent; a retry re-sends these exact bytes, never regenerated content, so a hash mismatch is detectable. event_sequence bigint NOT NULL — copied once from phase1_partner_notification_sequences at allocation time, immutable afterward. expires_at timestamptz NOT NULL.

delivery_target varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'partner_endpoint' CHECK (delivery_target = 'partner_endpoint'). delivery_stage varchar(20) NULL CHECK (delivery_stage IN ('outbox_persisted','partner_accepted','provider_accepted','device_received','opened')) — null until a completed attempt sets it; this design version's own code paths may only ever write 'partner_accepted' or leave it null on failure — 'provider_accepted'/'device_received'/'opened' are reserved for a future, separately versioned device-callback task and must not be written speculatively.

retry_disposition varchar(30) NULL CHECK (retry_disposition IN ('automatic','configuration_blocked','manual_only','terminal','none')), failure_reason varchar(50) NULL CHECK (failure_reason IN ('configuration_blocked','endpoint_disabled','route_missing','route_ambiguous','owner_changed','recipient_revoked','provider_transient_error','credential_rejected','endpoint_unavailable','partner_ack_invalid','notification_expired','notification_obsolete','notification_superseded')) — set together from one completed attempt's outcome, per PARTNER_NOTIFICATION_FAILURE_REASON_RETRY_DISPOSITIONS in packages/contracts/src/partner-passenger-notification.ts; a worker selecting rows to retry must filter on the existing outbox status, next_attempt_at, this retry_disposition and expires_at together — reading outbox status alone would let a generic worker infinitely re-scan configuration_blocked/manual_only/terminal rows (design §9).

receipt_id text NULL — must equal the partner's own response receipt_id (design §7); never a synthesized value such as 'receipt-' || outbox_id. A schema-reconciliation test should assert no row's receipt_id matches that synthetic pattern, since apps/api/src/modules/multi-taxi/passenger-push.adapter.ts:264's existing synthetic-receipt fallback is exactly the anti-pattern this column forbids for the partner transport (out of this task's write scope to fix; downstream transport task's job).

downstream_status varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown' CHECK (downstream_status = 'unknown') — first version never writes any other value; adding delivered/opened values is a future, separately versioned callback task's decision, not this migration's.

created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), delivered_at timestamptz NULL — delivered_at is set only when this transport's own ack validation completes (design §7), never the attempt's start time and never the partner's self-reported time.

Fencing ownership: ops.consumer_notification_outbox (existing, unchanged) retains sole claim/fence/retry-timer ownership; this table records receipt/outcome inside that same fence transaction (design §8 point 6) and introduces no second claim mechanism or independent retry timer.

table_invariants: iam.phase1_passenger_push_devices: device_id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() — server-generated only. drts_passenger_id varchar(100) NOT NULL, platform varchar(10) NOT NULL CHECK (platform IN ('ios','android')), provider varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'fcm_v1' CHECK (provider = 'fcm_v1') — fixed for v1, matches PassengerPushDeviceProvider in packages/contracts/src/passenger-notification-channel.ts.

app_id varchar(150) NOT NULL, app_version varchar(50) NOT NULL, token text NOT NULL, token_sha256 varchar(64) NOT NULL — the token column exists for the transport to actually call FCM with; application code must never log it or return it from any API response, only device_id or the first 8 characters of token_sha256 (design doc D4). No table-wide UNIQUE(provider, token_sha256): the re-registration rule below inserts a new row while the prior row (same hash) survives as 'revoked', so a full-table unique constraint on every row would reject that insert. Uniqueness is instead a partial index limited to currently-active rows: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX phase1_passenger_push_devices_active_token_uq ON iam.phase1_passenger_push_devices (provider, token_sha256) WHERE status = 'active' — at most one 'active' row per (provider, token_sha256) at a time; any number of historical 'revoked'/'invalid' rows may share a hash.
status varchar(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('active','revoked','invalid')), status_reason text NULL, notification_consent_version varchar(50) NOT NULL.

registered_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), last_seen_at timestamptz NULL, invalidated_at timestamptz NULL, created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() — a device past 60 days without last_seen_at is unusable for selection but is never deleted by this migration; row deletion is out of scope.

Re-registration transaction: re-registering an already-bound token_sha256 under a different drts_passenger_id must, in one transaction, set the prior row's status='revoked' (status_reason recording the hand-off) and insert a new row for the new passenger — never UPDATE drts_passenger_id in place on the existing row, preserving the historical binding for audit. This is only possible because uniqueness is enforced by the partial index above (WHERE status='active'), not a table-wide UNIQUE: as soon as the prior row's status flips to 'revoked' inside the same transaction, it drops out of the partial index and the new 'active' row with the same (provider, token_sha256) is admitted. A token rotation likewise inserts a new row and revokes the old one rather than overwriting the token/token_sha256 columns of an existing row (content-identity immutable, same precedent as V0098's remittance-proof content fields).

Active-device cap: a transaction that would leave a passenger with more than 10 'active' rows must first revoke the 'active' row with the oldest last_seen_at (nulls treated as oldest) for that drts_passenger_id, enforced in application logic, not a DB trigger, consistent with this ledger's existing precedent of application-layer transaction invariants (e.g. V0098, V0100).

receipt_id text NULL — must equal FCM's own response message name (design D6); never a synthesized value. created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), delivered_at timestamptz NULL — set only when this transport's own ack validation completes, never the attempt's start time or FCM's self-reported time.

A disputed decision, its linked crm complaint and initial timeline commit or roll back together. Existing payout amounts and calculation algorithms are unchanged.

Backfill only same-event non-null canonical duty actor/time; preserve delivery/render as distinct transitions. Root reserved V0124 after existing Voice V0122 and Complaint V0123 reservations.

complaint_command_allocations.description: Durable cross-process pending-commit identity for an ordinary (non-settlement) complaint mutation whose COMMIT outcome was left unknown, so a same-logical-command retry recovers the originally allocated caseNo/entryId after an API restart or on a different replica instead of only within the originating process's in-memory pendingUncertainCommits Map.
table_invariants: crm.phase1_complaint_pending_commits: command_key varchar(64) PRIMARY KEY. Identified callers hash stableStringify([action, original caller scope, trimmed original key]); legacy unkeyed commands hash action + colon + caseNo + colon + stableStringify(matchCommand). The original payload is bound separately, so distinct keyed intents remain distinct and a changed payload under one key conflicts.

case_no varchar(100) NOT NULL, action varchar(100) NOT NULL, command_payload jsonb NOT NULL (the original matchCommand, re-hydrated into PendingUncertainComplaintCommit.matchCommand on recovery so the existing stableStringify comparison keeps working verbatim), case_snapshot jsonb NOT NULL, timeline_snapshot jsonb NOT NULL, previous_case_snapshot jsonb NULL (NULL for a create-type action; the update-type actions' pre-mutation snapshot otherwise, used to rebuild the existing in-memory revertComplaintCaseMutation rollback instead of a non-serializable closure).
status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending','confirmed','failed')), created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now().
CREATE INDEX idx_phase1_complaint_pending_commits_case_no ON crm.phase1_complaint_pending_commits (case_no) — reconcilePendingCase's existing durable-store sweep scans by case_no.

Write timing: mandatory durable PREPARED reservation is awaited before the ordinary business transaction can begin. The winning original caseNo, timeline entry IDs, caller identity and payload are preserved; reservation failure cannot acknowledge or issue a business COMMIT. The same transaction locks the prepared row and atomically confirms it with canonical case/timeline writes. Confirmed keyed results remain durable for original-result replay without another upsert; unknown outcomes preserve their original reservation. Only a definitely rejected new preparation or a reconciled legacy result is eligible for its own bounded cleanup; a missing or failed read cannot prove an unknown COMMIT rolled back.

complaint_command_allocations.description: USER policy: every new score 1/2 creates its canonical case and initial timeline independently of immutable contact choice. Capture pre-existing consent case requirements and pre-existing rating policy provenance without backfilling cases or contact. New missing provenance fails closed.
table_invariants: Existing consent rows capture case_required from their existing non-null case reference; new consent writes explicitly provide case_required with no database default. Equality with presence of the original FK-bound case is mandatory. Token case-required rows retain rating_score <= 2. Existing FK, unique, subject, score and immutable request constraints are retained.

Existing rating rows capture low_rating_case_policy_v2=false. Subsequent rows have a NOT NULL true default; only explicit historical false permits the original omitted-contact retry without a consent row. Missing/unknown provenance never establishes legacy consent or permits a new missing case.

contact_requested remains the original immutable passenger choice. A false low-rating choice still has a canonical case and timeline with an explicit no-contact description; internal audit/SLA handling does not imply passenger contact.

referral_passenger_journey_allocations.description: R6 normal reservation after V0126: immutable referral-owned taxi-policy estimates and atomic consumption; explicitly identify pre-existing referral ratings as legacy without creating cases or changing their contact choice.
table_invariants: Quote ownership is the exact verified tenant/partner/program/entry/passenger tuple; no passenger.accounts FK or fabricated pre-order owned order.
Only consumed order/time can change. Quote consumption, original order/intent and notification route commit together.

New referral ratings require explicit policy provenance and score<=2 canonical case/timeline regardless of contact preference. Migration marks only pre-existing rating objects legacy; missing provenance is not legacy.

normal_onboarding_supply_pair_allocation.description: Normal approval of an explicit same-fleet approved driver reference creates the structural vehicle-driver pair. Unknown onboarding ETA is NULL, never a fabricated zero/five-minute measurement; only the existing ETA column nullability changes.
table_invariants: Only eta_minutes nullability changes; all existing rows, pair keys and other columns remain unchanged.
Pair, canonical vehicle and submission approval/document/event writes use the existing single transaction. Publish the new local pair only after successful COMMIT.
Existing numeric legacy ETA values preserve their behavior; a new NULL estimate without driver observation/destination does not create a zero-minute candidate.
All license, contract, insurance, exclusivity, workstate, product and location checks remain unchanged.

Order/quote/fee snapshot/normal notification route share the existing transaction and owned quote; server time, disclosure hash and real quote tariff kept distinct.
Exact committed old intent can replay without fee backfill; no historical quote-consumption/creation/privacy time is transformed into fee agreement.

referral_monthly_rating_governance_alloc.description: Traffic Bureau R04 monthly driver rating coaching (< 4.0) and three-consecutive-month low rating (< 3.5) termination review governance records with audited handling outcomes.
table_invariants: UNIQUE (driver_id, period_month, rule_type) enforces per-driver, per-Asia/Taipei-month, per-rule idempotency so coaching and termination_review records can both exist for the same driver and month without overwriting each other.

Idempotent evaluation upserts aggregate fields (average_rating, rating_count, consecutive_low_months, triggered_months, monthly_breakdown) while preserving recorded handling status, outcome, outcome_reason, handled_by_actor_id, handled_at and audit_id.

CHECK constraints enforce period_month YYYY-MM format, rule_type IN ('coaching', 'termination_review'), status IN ('pending', 'coached', 'terminated', 'dismissed'), and consistency between pending/null outcome and handled outcome/reason/actor/timestamp.
